notes: Face (chin to crown) must take up 70–80% of the photo height, i.e. 32–36 mm; head including hairstyle should be fully shown.
Background one colour and bright, ideally neutral grey (medium grey for light hair, light grey for dark hair); no pattern or shadows.
Glasses allowed if eyes clearly visible: no reflections, no tinted glasses or sunglasses, frames must not cover the eyes.
Neutral expression, mouth closed, looking straight into the camera; no headwear except for religious reasons.
Printed at least 600 dpi on high-quality paper.
Source is the Schengen visa photo sheet published by a German mission; individual Schengen consulates or visa centres may add their own wording (e.g. background colour).
Head (chin tip to crown) should take up approx. 2/3 of the image (≈30 mm of 45 mm, converted) and must not exceed 36 mm; high hairstyles may extend beyond the frame.
Eye distance (centre to centre) at least 8 mm, optimally 10 mm; head centred.
Background single-colour and light, ideally grey (medium grey for light hair, light grey for dark hair); no pattern or shadows.
Glasses allowed if eyes clearly visible; no reflections, tinted lenses or sunglasses; frames must not cover the eyes.
Colour photo only (B/W not accepted for passport, ID card, residence permit); not older than 6 months.
Children must be alone in the photo with face fully visible and eyes open.
Same criteria apply to residence permits and driving licences.
Face length (chin to crown) 31–36 mm, i.e. 70–80% of the photo height.
Background light-coloured, uniform, single colour, no gradient, with enough contrast to the head.
Glasses allowed if eyes fully visible, lenses fully transparent, no disturbing reflection or shadow; otherwise remove them.
Neutral expression, mouth closed, teeth not visible; colour photo (B/W not allowed for passports); max 6 months old; printed at min. 400 dpi.
Applies to passports, Kids-ID, eID and residence documents for foreigners.
Under 6: exempt from 'eyes on a horizontal line', 'head tilted', 'shoulders straight', 'neutral expression', 'looking into the camera' and 'mouth closed'.
Any support holding the child must not be visible.

Most applications (in Bulgaria and at equipped consulates) capture the face digitally at the counter; a printed photo is only needed where no digital capture is available (Regulation Art. 9(3), Art. 21(6)).
Rules from Annex 5 to the Regulation on Issuing Bulgarian Personal Documents (PMS No. 13/2010); applies to all Bulgarian personal documents.
Background: neutral light grey, 20% grey density (acceptable range 15 to 25%).
After trimming, 47 ± 2 mm × 37 ± 2 mm is tolerated.
Colour, taken within the last 2 years; smooth matte paper 0.12 to 0.20 mm thick; no glossy paper, scans or retouching.
Frontal, head centred, camera at eye level; even lighting, no shadows, glare or red-eye.
Glasses only if worn permanently, with untinted lenses and no reflections.
No hats or headscarves unless both ears and at least 1 cm of hair are visible.
For persons under 14, head height 25 to 35 mm.

Head (chin to crown) must fill 70 to 80% of the photo height (31.5 to 36 mm on 45 mm), per MUP/police guidance for the 2021 ID card; the passport and ID card regulations say about 2/3 of the photo and no more than 36 mm.
Background: single-colour light, no pattern, enough contrast with face and hair (Pravilnik NN 63/2015 and NN 4/2010).
Head centred; distance between eye centres at least 8 mm (optimally 10 mm).
Frontal (en face), forehead uncovered, neutral expression, eyes open, mouth closed.
No head covering except for religious or medical reasons, provided cheeks, chin and forehead stay visible.
Glasses are not prohibited; tinted glasses only for blind persons.
Children must be alone in the photo with the face fully visible and eyes open.
Colour photo on high-quality smooth glossy paper; no retouching and no photo-booth (automat) photos.
Passport sizes: 35×45 mm (putni list uses 30×35 mm). No photo needed if a passport or eID was issued in the last 5 years and appearance has not changed.
Regulations: https://narodne-novine.nn.hr/clanci/sluzbeni/full/2015_06_63_1213.html and https://zakon.hr/cms.htm?id=9557
Head 30–36 mm from tip of chin to top of hair.
Background without motifs, in a uniform light colour, e.g. light blue or light grey. People with white/light hair or a light headscarf need a background in sharp contrast.
Photo shows the face and the top of the shoulders, taken straight on; colour or black-and-white.
Glasses: eyes fully clear of frames, lenses not tinted and without reflections.
Head covering only for religious reasons; forehead, chin and cheekbones visible.
All rules also apply to children. Same police rules apply to driving licence photos.
ID card (legitimationskort) is issued by municipalities; e.g. Odense requires a photo meeting the police passport photo rules. Some municipalities take the photo at Borgerservice instead.
Area between chin and top of head must be 70–80% of the photo height (35–40 mm on a 50 mm photo).
Background flat, single colour, light; recommended light blue, beige, light brown, light grey or white, contrasting with face and hair.
Digital upload to the PPA self-service portal: colour, unedited, at least 1,300 × 1,600 px, file size between 1 MB and 5 MB (per politsei.ee).
Taken within 6 months; neutral expression, mouth closed, eyes open, no headgear or headphones.
Glasses allowed if frames do not cover the eyes and there are no reflections.
Young children (0–7): mouth closed, looking straight into the camera; avoid big hair adornments and toys.
Head size is measured from crown of head to chin EXCLUDING hair and beard: 445–500 px (32–36 mm). Hair need not be fully visible.
Above the crown: 56–84 px (4–6 mm). Below the chin: 96–124 px (7–9 mm). Face centre line within 21 px (1.5 mm) of photo centre line.
Digital photos (sent by the photographer to the police photo server) must be exactly 500 × 653 px, JPEG (not JPEG2000), max 250 KB.
Paper photo size 36 × 47 mm per Finnish Immigration Service (Migri) photo guidance; paper photos only accepted at a police service point.
Best background colour is light grey; must be monochrome, light, neutral, without shadows, and contrast with face, hair and clothes.
Same instructions apply to passports, identity cards and permits granted by the police (residence permits use the same rules).
Glasses allowed if frames are not near the eyes and there are no reflections; tinted glasses only for medical reasons.
An older Migri form allows a smaller head (min 25 mm) for children under 11; the 2020 police instructions state the same requirements apply to all ages.
Rules on a closed mouth are flexible for very young babies, but the mouth may only be slightly open.
Even small children must keep their eyes open.
A small child may be supported, but no part of the supporting person may be visible.
Face size 3.2–3.6 cm (70–80% of the photo) is measured from the bottom of the chin to the top of the skull, EXCLUDING hair.
Background must be plain and light-coloured (e.g. light blue or light grey); white background is forbidden.
Taken less than 6 months ago; must be taken by an approved professional photographer or approved booth.
Neutral expression, mouth closed, eyes open and visible, head bare, ears uncovered.
Glasses optional; if worn, thin frames not masking the eyes, lenses not tinted and without reflection.
Colour photo strongly recommended.
Optimal face height (chin to top of head) 32–36 mm for ages 10 and over, per the BMI/Bundesdruckerei Lichtbild-Schablone.
Background uniform single colour, preferably light grey.
Colour only for digital photos; neutral expression, lips closed, eyes open and not covered.
Glasses allowed if the eyes remain recognisable and uncovered (no reflections or tinted lenses).

Since 1 May 2025 passports, ID cards and electronic residence permits accept only digital photos taken at the authority or uploaded by a certified photo service via cloud; paper photos only for exceptions.
Same rules apply to the electronic residence permit (eAT).
Children 6–9 years: optimal face height 22–36 mm.
Children up to 5 years: no biometric check required; only size (35 × 45 mm), frontal pose, sharpness/contrast, lighting, background and photo quality apply (so eyes/expression are relaxed).
Printed-photo spec (used for applications abroad). Chin to crown 31–35 mm, face width ear to ear 20–25 mm, eye line 30–39 mm from bottom.
Background light, preferably grey RGB (190,190,190) ±10; older printed spec also allows white or cream.
In Greece the photo is submitted digitally via gov.gr myPhoto: JPEG, 1280 × 1600 px (4:5), max 3 MB.
Printed at 1200 dpi or more; not inkjet/laser; taken recently.
Wear glasses if normally worn: clear lenses, no reflections, frames not covering eyes; tinted/photochromic lenses not allowed.
Neutral expression, mouth closed, eyes normally open.
For children under 12 and infants, face dimensions may reasonably be smaller than the adult values and are accepted.
Head size from ICAO guidance; DFA gives no head measurement, only 'head to mid torso' with visible space between head/shoulders and photo edge.
Print size: minimum 35 × 45 mm, maximum 38 × 50 mm. Paper applications need 4 identical photos, no more than 6 months old.
Background: completely plain light grey, white or cream, with enough contrast.
Online (Passport Book or Passport Card): colour JPEG, at least 715 × 951 px, no larger than 9 MB, not scanned, no compression artefacts, no selfies.
Passport Card is applied for online only and uses the same photo guidelines.
Clear glasses allowed if frames do not cover eyes and no glare; no sunglasses/dark glasses.
Neutral expression, mouth closed, no red-eye, no shadows; head covering only for religious or medical reasons.
An infant or very young child who cannot support themselves should be photographed lying down on a plain white surface.
Hands or arms supporting the child must not be visible; no soothers/pacifiers.
For babies and small children (newborn to 36 months) the online system may ask you to frame the face manually with its cropping tool.
Guardians should make every effort to ensure the child is not smiling and mouth is not open.
Carta d'Identità Elettronica (CIE). Width 35 mm, minimum height 45 mm.
Source states face height 70–80% of photo height; converted to 31.5–36 mm on a 45 mm photo.
Eye height from the bottom edge between 23 and 31 mm.
Background uniform, preferably light blue, beige, light brown, light grey or white.
Digital photo on USB: JPG, at least 400 dpi, max 500 KB.
Taken within 6 months; no tinted lenses; neutral expression, mouth closed.
Source states face covers 70–80% of the photo (measured chin base to forehead); converted to 31.5–36 mm on a 45 mm photo.
Polizia di Stato leaflet gives width 35–40 mm (no height); 35 × 45 mm is the size stated by Italian embassies.
White background with even lighting; colour, taken within 6 months.
Neutral expression, mouth closed, eyes open; no tinted lenses, heavy frames or flash reflections on glasses.
Head coverings only for religious reasons, with face from chin to forehead visible.
Submit a 40 × 60 mm print sheet with at least 3 identical photos; the office cuts each to 35 × 45 mm, so the 35 × 45 area must hold all the distances.
Chin to top of head 70–80% of the cut photo height (31–35 mm); 2–4 mm from top edge to top of head; 8–10 mm from chin to bottom edge.
Background very light, single-colour and even; use a darker background if hair is very light.
People who always wear glasses are photographed with them; no tinted or coloured lenses, frames must not cover the eyes.
Black-and-white print recommended for ID card, passport and residence permit.
Recommended to be taken no more than 6 months before applying.
Same rules apply to the residence permit and other personal documents.
Pose and expression rules may be waived for children under 6.
Children under 1 may be held, lying down or seated, on a light, single-colour, even background.
Luxembourg MFA requires photos to meet ICAO quality standards and links the ISO/ICAO photo guidelines: face 70–80% of the photo = 32–36 mm chin to crown.
Background one colour and bright, ideally neutral grey; no pattern or shadows.
Glasses allowed if eyes clearly visible; no reflections, tinted glasses or sunglasses; frames must not cover eyes.
In Luxembourg the ID photo is usually taken on the spot by the issuing office (e.g. Bierger-Center); a printed photo matters mainly for special cases.
Print resolution at least 600 dpi.
Photo matrix model 2020: face height from chin to crown 26–30 mm (age 11+); face width ear-base to ear-base 16–20 mm.
Background grey, light blue or white; plain, single colour, no gradient or shadow, enough contrast with the head.
Glasses allowed if eyes fully visible, lenses fully transparent, no disturbing reflection or shadow; otherwise remove them.
Colour, max 6 months old, not edited, printed on smooth photo paper at min. 400 dpi; mouth closed, neutral expression.
Also used for Dutch driving licences.
Up to and including age 10: face height chin to crown 19–30 mm.
Under 6: exempt from horizontal eyes, head tilt, straight shoulders, neutral expression, looking into camera and mouth closed; any support must not be visible.
Head size converted from the source: face must fill 70–80% of the photo (31.5–36 mm of 45 mm).
Whole head from the crown plus top of the shoulders.
White, evenly lit background without shadows.
Corrective glasses allowed if eyes are clearly visible, frames do not cover eyebrows and lenses show no reflections; dark glasses only with a disability certificate.
Taken no earlier than 6 months before applying.
Online application: colour digital photo, min 492 × 633 px, max 2.5 MB, 35 × 45 proportions. At the office: 35 × 45 mm colour print.
Children under 5 may have closed eyes, open mouth or an unnatural expression.
Face must be uncovered (no hair or toys), head straight, background light and uniform with no other people.
Head size converted from the source: face must fill 70–80% of the photo (31.5–36 mm of 45 mm).
Whole head from the crown plus top of the shoulders.
White, evenly lit background without shadows.
Corrective glasses allowed if eyes are clearly visible, frames do not cover eyebrows and lenses show no reflections; dark glasses only with a disability certificate.
Taken no earlier than 6 months before applying.
Digital rules (min 768 × 1004 px, max 2.5 MB, colour, 35 × 45 proportions) apply only to online applications for children under 12; at the office submit a 35 × 45 mm colour print.
Children under 5 may have closed eyes, open mouth or an unnatural expression.
Face must be uncovered (no hair or toys), head straight, background light and uniform with no other people.
Chin to crown 70–80% of the photo (32–36 mm); with voluminous hair the face must not be under 32 mm.
Eye line converted from the source: 50–70% of photo height from the bottom edge (22.5–31.5 mm).
Background single-colour and light, ideally neutral grey; medium grey for light hair, light grey for dark hair; no patterns or shadows.
Glasses allowed without reflections; frames must not cover the eyes; no tinted lenses or sunglasses except for medical reasons.
Print on white thin glossy photo paper, at least 600 dpi, colour or black-and-white; photo-booth photos are not accepted.
Neutral expression, mouth closed, looking straight at the camera.

ID card applications in Slovenia need an e-fotograf reference number from an authorised photographer; paper photos are accepted for the ID card only abroad at embassies/consulates or in exceptional cases. Passport applications accept a paper photo.
Children under 10: face 50–80% of the photo (22–36 mm, crown without hairstyle); eye line may go down to 40% of photo height (18 mm).
Children must have mouth closed, no other people in the background, no toys near the face.
Under 3: deviations in head posture, expression, gaze and centring allowed, but the photo must be frontal and a baby's eyes must be open.
